name: St. Veit in Defereggen
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Defereggental valley, featuring a late Gothic parish church and sunlit alpine meadows.
beschreibung:
Überblick

St. Veit in Defereggen is situated in the East Tyrolean district of Lienz on a sun-drenched terrace high above the Schwarzach river along the southern slopes of the Lasörling Group. With its village centre and parish church standing at 1,495 metres above sea level, St. Veit is the highest health resort village and highest-altitude municipality in East Tyrol, with municipal territory extending from the valley floor at around 1,008 metres up to high alpine peaks above 2,900 metres. Approximately 650 residents reside across picturesque mountain farming hamlets such as Görtschach, Gassen, Gritzen, Moos, and Bruggen. Sheltered from harsh valley winds, St. Veit boasts one of the highest sunshine records in the Eastern Alps and holds the status of a certified climatic health resort, presenting breathtaking panoramic vistas across the glaciated Rieserferner Group and the Villgraten Mountains.

Geschichte

The first documented mention dates to 29 October 1313, when the settlement was recorded as 'Sanctus Vitus' in a land register of the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg. For more than five centuries, the entire Defereggental valley belonged ecclesiastically and territorially to Salzburg rather than Tyrol, an affiliation that shaped local timber architecture and customs until secularisation in 1803. A tragic historical episode occurred in the winter of 1684/85 with the expulsion of Defereggen's Protestant population under Archbishop Max Gandolf von Kuenburg, which forced around 650 inhabitants to leave their homeland; the church's 'Protestant Bell', cast in 1635, commemorates this event. Due to barren alpine soils, generations of local men travelled across Europe as peddlers ('Kraxenträger') trading in hats and goods. The village's most renowned native is priest and folk author Sebastian Rieger (1867–1953), known under the pen name 'Reimmichl', whose heartwarming stories and widely read annual calendar made him a literary icon of Tyrol.

Anreise

By car, travel from the north via Kitzbühel or Mittersill along the Felbertauernstraße B108 (through the Felbertauern tunnel) to Huben in East Tyrol. At Huben, branch off onto the Defereggentalstraße (L25) and take the ascending scenic road up to the sunny plateau of St. Veit. From the south or east, approach via Spittal an der Drau on the Drautalstraße B100 to Lienz, continuing on the B108 to Huben. By rail, arrive at Lienz in Osttirol railway station on the Drautal line. From the station forecourt, VVT regional bus route 954 runs regularly through Huben into the Defereggental valley, with connecting services up to St. Veit's church square.

Tipps

A stroll along the themed Reimmichl trail begins at the village square beside the bronze Reimmichl fountain, leading past the author's birthplace while highlighting traditional rural heritage. Ambitious hikers should climb the Speikboden (2,653 m), the village's panoramic mountain, rewarding summiteers with a magnificent 360-degree vista of more than sixty 3,000-metre peaks including the Großglockner, Großvenediger, and the Drei Zinnen. Tucked away in a pristine glacial cirque beneath the peak lie the two emerald Gritzer Seen lakes (2,504 m). Following a hike, enjoy an authentic mountain meal at the Speikbodenhütte or Gritzer Alm, sampling home-made East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen dumplings. Cultural enthusiasts should not miss the parish church of St. Vitus to admire its 15th-century Gothic choir frescoes.
